speaker: Doctor
text: I need to understand the progression of your symptoms better. When did the difficulty walking, urinary incontinence, and speech issues first begin, and have they been getting worse over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the combination of progressive gait difficulty, urinary incontinence, and recent speech slurring, I need to assess for potential spinal cord compression or other neurological deficits. Have you noticed any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your legs or arms? REQUEST TEST: MRI Cervical Spine and Lumbar Spine.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive difficulty walking. I also have Urinary incontinence, Slurred speech, Rigidity in limbs, Mild hand tremor, Orthostatic hypotension. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Cellulitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Multiple System Atrophy (Shy-Drager Syndrome). The patient's presentation of progressive gait difficulty, urinary incontinence, speech slurring, rigidity, tremor, and orthostatic hypotension is classic for MSA-C or MSA-P, not cellulitis.
